newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait share index up, dealers see upward trend.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait share index up, dealers see upward trend.

text.p: Kuwait share index rose 61.4 points to 2,297.3 in the three-day week to Wednesday as the stock market appeared to be in an upward cycle, dealers said on Thursday.

"It seems that we are entering a new cycle now. The market corrected for a few weeks and that is over now," said a dealer. "Most companies are showing good performance and investors have cash," he added.
The market adjusted for a few weaks after big rises in the first quarter of 1997 fuelled by expectations of high annual profits by listed firms.
In the week, which was shortened by the Moslem Eid al-Adha holiday, losers led gainers 39-8, while 18 shares did not move.

The daily average for value of traded shares rose to 67 million dinars ($221 million) from 40 million. Volume rose to a daily average of 234 million shares from 163 million, figures released by the Kuwait Stock Exchange on Thursday show.
"Now Eid is finished activity would increase as long as other factors remain to be positive," said a portfolio manager.
In the first quarter of 1997 the index and trade levels registered several peaks mainly due to capital flows from abroad to invest in listed firms that showed profit increases in 1996.
Investment firms were the most active sector in terms of traded value with 96 million dinars, followed by real estate firms with 55 million and banks with 24 million.
United Realty, Kuwait Real Estate, Investment Projects, National Imnvestment and Gulf Bank were among the most active shares.
Only nationals of Gulf Arab states -- Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Kuwait -- can trade on the exchange. Foreign residents can invest in mutual funds.
